advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename the new `resign.classify_plan_review_attestation` (e.g. `classify_review_attestation_outcome`) to avoid colliding with the differently-typed `bugfix_size_gate.classify_plan_review_attestation`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:160: `def classify_plan_review_attestation(ticket_id: str, repo_root: Any = None, state: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:`

The two have unrelated semantics: bsg's returns `{verdict, reason}` classifying whether an attested review was COMPLETED (bugfix_size_gate.py:163-170); the new one returns a `PlanReviewAttestation` classifying whether a PASS left a signature behind.
They are never co-imported (mcp/cli import the resign one; bsg is called via module attribute), so there is no runtime shadowing — this is a clarity/navigation concern only.
advisory.finding: A second function named `classify_plan_review_attestation` already exists in `rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` with a different signature, return type, and meaning than the new one added to `resign.py`; the identical name across two modules in the same package is a navigation/maintenance hazard.
scenarios: A reader greps `classify_plan_review_attestation` and lands on the wrong module.
A future refactor imports the wrong symbol given identical names and both being plausibly 'the' plan-review attestation classifier.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `classify_plan_review_attestation` returns cause='relation_unreadable' and recovery_tool='review_plan' for a `plan_review_sign_aborted` signature whose error is in `PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS` (e.g. 'store-read-failure'), and add that row to the CLI/MCP parity CASES table.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:522-541 introduces the `_is_relation_read_failure` branch returning `cause=ATTESTATION_RELATION_UNREADABLE, recovery_tool="review_plan"` with a distinct message
search for 'relation_unreadable' across tests/ returned (no matches)

CASES table (test_attestation_parity_heldout_2e16.py:36-50) covers signed / deliberate skip / sign failed / plan changed / no signature block, but omits any `plan_review_sign_aborted` + reason-in-REASONS case

The diff's stated purpose: 'When the plan CHANGED or the relation snapshot is unreadable, re-signing would hit the same state and refuse, so the agent is sent to `review_plan` instead ... a test fails if it ever does.' — but no test drives the relation-unreadable path
advisory.finding: The new `relation_unreadable` classification branch — a distinct structured output the diff adds specifically so the MCP surface preserves bug 94a3's no-refusal-loop rule — has no test asserting its `cause` ('relation_unreadable') or its `recovery_tool` ('review_plan'). A regression flipping that branch to `recovery_tool='sign_review'` (the exact refusal loop the ticket claims to prevent for MCP) would pass all new tests.
scenarios: A future edit to `_is_relation_read_failure` or the relation branch that mis-routes relation-read failures to `sign_review`
REASONS vocabulary drift (relation_snapshot.PlanRelationSnapshotError.REASONS) silently no longer matching, downgrading the branch to generic sign_failed advice on the agent-facing MCP payload
advisory.suggested_fix: Add to CASES: ("relation unreadable", {"signed": False, "error": "store-read-failure", "event": "plan_review_sign_aborted"}, True); and a dedicated test asserting got.cause == 'relation_unreadable' and got.recovery_tool == 'review_plan'.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 263 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 2e16-cd19-2323-4ae2 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 2e16-cd19-2323-4ae2` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 2e16-cd19-2323-4ae2` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 2e16-cd19-2323-4ae2 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
